drug_class: Antiretroviral combination (HIV integrase inhibitor + non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor)
purpose: This medication is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults who are already stable on another HIV treatment. It helps keep the amount of HIV virus in your blood very low (undetectable). Having an undetectable viral load means you stay healthier and greatly lowers the chance of spreading HIV to others.
how_it_works: HIV needs to make copies of itself to survive in your body. Cabotegravir blocks a tool the virus uses called integrase, which stops the virus from inserting itself into your cells. Rilpivirine blocks another tool the virus uses to copy itself. Together, these two medicines team up to keep the virus under very tight control.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are pain, soreness, swelling, or a hard lump at the injection site. You may also feel tired, have a headache, fever, or feel dizzy. Some people feel nauseous or have trouble sleeping. These effects are usually mild and get better over time.
warnings: Never miss or skip your injection appointments — missing doses can allow the virus to become resistant, meaning the medicine may stop working. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver problems, including hepatitis B or C, because this drug can affect your liver. Do not take certain other medications (like some seizure drugs or rifampin) as they can make this medicine work less well. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor right away. Rarely, serious allergic reactions can occur — seek emergency care if you have rash, trouble breathing, or swelling of the face.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as two separate injections (shots) by your healthcare provider in a clinic or office — one shot of cabotegravir and one shot of rilpivirine, both given into your buttock muscle. After starting injections, you receive them once a month or once every two months, depending on the schedule your doctor chooses. You cannot give these shots to yourself at home — you must keep all your clinic appointments.
